about: Frame n is drawn at n × 1000 / fps ms from the run's start, and a step at t ms takes effect before the first frame whose time is t or later. The input is the step's time and the frame rate; the answer is {frame}.

vectors.name: a step at 100 ms first shows in frame 6 at 60 fps
a step at 100 ms first shows in frame 12 at 120 fps
a step at 0 ms shows in frame 0
a step just after frame 6's time waits for frame 7
a step at 16 ms shows in frame 1 (16.7 ms)
a step at 17 ms, after frame 1's time, waits for frame 2
a record script's event at frame 7 at 60 fps, at floor(7000 / 60) = 116 ms, lands before frame 7
at 1 fps a step at 1000 ms shows in frame 1
at 1 fps a step at 999 ms shows in frame 1
